doc.name: VLT Midi Drive FC 280 Programming Guide

faults.name: Live zero error
faults.meaning: The signal on analog input 53 or 54 has fallen below 50% of the low end configured for that input (par. 6-10, 6-20 or 6-22).
checks: Check wiring and connectors on terminals 53/54 and the signal source
Compare the live signal with the low-voltage/low-current scaling in 6-10, 6-20, 6-22
Review live-zero timeout settings 6-00 and 6-01

faults.name: No motor
faults.meaning: No motor is detected on the drive output.
checks: Check that the motor cable is connected at both the drive and the motor
Check for an open motor circuit or contactor in the output

faults.name: Mains phase loss
faults.meaning: A supply phase is missing or the supply voltage imbalance is too high. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Measure all three supply phases and the voltage balance at the drive input
Check input fuses, contactor and supply cables
Consider a line filter if the supply is distorted
See par. 14-12 for the imbalance reaction

faults.name: DC overvoltage
faults.meaning: The DC-link voltage has exceeded its limit. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration ramp or enable over-voltage control (2-17)
Check for an overhauling load or regenerative energy; add brake resistor if needed
Check supply voltage level and quality; consider a line filter

faults.name: DC undervoltage
faults.meaning: The DC-link voltage has dropped below the low-voltage warning limit. Mains distortion can also cause it.
checks: Measure the supply voltage and check for sags or dips
Check input fuses and contactors for voltage drop under load
Consider a line filter if the supply is distorted

faults.name: Inverter overloaded
faults.meaning: The drive has been carrying more than 100% load for too long.
checks: Compare motor current (16-14) and inverter thermal (16-35) with the rating
Reduce the load or use a larger drive
Check ramp times and the switching frequency setting (14-01)

faults.name: Motor ETR overtemperature
faults.meaning: The electronic thermal model says the motor is too hot after running above 100% load too long.
checks: Check actual motor load and cooling
Verify motor nameplate current in 1-24 and the thermal protection setting in 1-90
Look at motor thermal readout 16-18

faults.name: Motor thermistor overtemperature
faults.meaning: The thermistor or its wiring is disconnected, or the motor is overheated.
checks: Check the thermistor wiring and connection to the selected input (1-93)
Check motor cooling and load
Verify the digital input mode (5-00) matches the thermistor wiring

faults.name: Torque limit
faults.meaning: Torque has exceeded the motor-mode limit (4-16) or generator-mode limit (4-17).
checks: Check load and mechanical binding
Review the limits in 4-16 and 4-17
Lengthen the ramp times if the limit is hit during acceleration or deceleration

faults.name: Overcurrent
faults.meaning: The inverter peak current limit was exceeded. If it appears at power-up, power cables may be wired to the motor terminals by mistake.
checks: Check that the supply cables are not connected to the motor terminals
Check motor and cable insulation and that the motor data matches the nameplate (1-2*)
Lengthen the acceleration ramp or reduce the load
Check for a locked or jammed mechanism

faults.name: Ground fault
faults.meaning: Current is leaking from the output phases to ground.
checks: Disconnect the motor and megger the cable and motor to earth
Check for damp or damaged motor cable and motor winding insulation
Check any output filter or long cable runs

faults.name: Short circuit
faults.meaning: There is a short circuit in the motor or at the motor terminals.
checks: Disconnect the motor and test phase-to-phase resistance of the cable and winding
Check the motor terminal box and connections for damage

faults.name: Control word timeout
faults.meaning: The drive is no longer receiving communication from the master.
checks: Check the fieldbus or serial cable and the master's status
Review timeout time and function (8-03 and 8-04)
Verify the protocol, address and baud rate settings (8-3*)

faults.name: Brake resistor short-circuited
faults.meaning: The brake resistor is shorted, so the brake function has been disabled.
checks: Disconnect and measure the brake resistor and its cable
Check the resistor value against 2-11

faults.name: Brake overload
faults.meaning: Power sent to the brake resistor over the last 120 s exceeded the allowed limit.
checks: Reduce regenerative energy with a lower speed or longer deceleration ramp
Check brake resistor ratings (2-11, 2-12)
Check the braking duty cycle

faults.name: Brake IGBT/chopper short-circuited
faults.meaning: The brake transistor is shorted, so the brake function has been disabled.
checks: Remove the brake resistor and power-cycle to test
If the alarm persists the drive needs service; contact the supplier

faults.name: Brake check
faults.meaning: The brake resistor is not connected or not working.
checks: Check brake resistor wiring and continuity
Check the resistor value in 2-11

faults.name: Motor phase U missing
faults.meaning: Motor output phase U is not present.
checks: Check the U wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

faults.name: Motor phase V missing
faults.meaning: Motor output phase V is not present.
checks: Check the V wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

faults.name: Motor phase W missing
faults.meaning: Motor output phase W is not present.
checks: Check the W wiring, terminals and any output contactor or filter
Measure winding resistance between phases

faults.name: Fieldbus fault
faults.meaning: PROFIBUS communication problems have occurred.
checks: Check the bus cable, terminations and connectors
Check master configuration and address
Check for EMC interference on the bus

faults.name: Option fault
faults.meaning: The fieldbus option reports internal faults.
checks: Power-cycle the drive
Check that the option card is seated correctly
Contact the supplier if it repeats

faults.name: Mains failure
faults.meaning: Active only when the supply voltage is below the level in 14-11 and 14-10 is not set to No function.
checks: Check the supply voltage and for dips or outages
Review 14-10 and 14-11

faults.name: Internal fault
faults.meaning: An internal drive fault has occurred.
checks: Note the fault reason in 15-31
Power-cycle the drive
Contact the local Danfoss supplier

faults.name: Overload on terminal 27
faults.meaning: The digital output on terminal 27 is overloaded.
checks: Check the load connected to terminal 27
Remove any short circuit on the terminal

faults.name: Gate drive voltage fault
faults.meaning: A fault in the gate-drive supply of the power card has been detected.
checks: Power-cycle the drive
Check for control-terminal shorts that overload internal supplies
Contact the supplier if it repeats

faults.name: 24 V supply low
faults.meaning: The 24 V DC supply may be overloaded.
checks: Check the load on the control terminals (24 V outputs)
Look for shorts or overloaded options

faults.name: Speed limit
faults.meaning: Motor speed is below the trip speed low limit set in 1-87.
checks: Check the load and settings in 1-87
Check for mechanical binding or a stalled motor

faults.name: AMA calibration failed
faults.meaning: A calibration error occurred during the automatic motor adaptation.
checks: Check motor data entered in 1-2* against the nameplate
Check motor cable and connections, then repeat AMA on a cold motor

faults.name: AMA check Unom and Inom
faults.meaning: The motor voltage and/or motor current settings are wrong.
checks: Re-enter voltage and current from the motor nameplate (1-22, 1-24)

faults.name: AMA low Inom
faults.meaning: The motor current is too low for AMA.
checks: Check the motor current setting (1-24) and the motor connection

faults.name: AMA big motor
faults.meaning: The motor is too large for AMA to run.
checks: Check that the drive is rated suitably for the motor
Enter the motor data manually

faults.name: AMA small motor
faults.meaning: The motor is too small for AMA to run.
checks: Check that the motor size matches the drive
Enter the motor data manually

faults.name: AMA parameter range
faults.meaning: Motor parameter values are outside the acceptable range, so AMA does not run.
checks: Recheck the nameplate data entered in 1-2*

faults.name: AMA interrupt
faults.meaning: The AMA was interrupted.
checks: Do not press stop or remove the run signal during AMA
Repeat the AMA

faults.name: AMA timeout
faults.meaning: The AMA timed out.
checks: Repeat AMA and check motor data and connection

faults.name: AMA internal
faults.meaning: An internal fault occurred during AMA.
checks: Contact Danfoss or the supplier

faults.name: Current limit
faults.meaning: The drive is overloaded and has reached its current limit.
checks: Reduce the load or lengthen the acceleration ramp
Check current limit setting 4-18
Check for jammed mechanics

faults.name: External interlock
faults.meaning: The external interlock input has been activated.
checks: Check the circuit wired to the digital input programmed as external interlock
Clear the cause, then reset

faults.name: Encoder loss
faults.meaning: The encoder or feedback signal was lost.
checks: Check encoder wiring, supply and settings in 4-3*

faults.name: Mechanical brake low
faults.meaning: The motor current did not reach the brake release current within the start delay.
checks: Check the release brake current setting (2-20) and the start delay
Check the motor connection and that the current can build up

faults.name: Control card temperature
faults.meaning: The control card cut-out temperature has exceeded its upper limit.
checks: Check the ambient temperature and cabinet ventilation
Check fans and filters; clean heatsink airways
Read the control card temperature in 16-39

faults.name: Option change
faults.meaning: A new option has been detected or a fitted one removed.
checks: Confirm the option change is intended, then reset
Check the option card seating

faults.name: Safe Torque Off
faults.meaning: STO has been activated. In manual restart mode, restore 24 V DC to terminals 37 and 38 and give a reset; in automatic restart mode, applying 24 V resumes operation. This alarm cannot be auto-reset through 14-20.
checks: Check the safety circuit feeding terminals 37 and 38
Restore 24 V DC on both terminals
Apply a reset via fieldbus, digital input or the [Reset] key (if manual restart)
Review 5-19 for the STO reaction

faults.name: Power card temperature
faults.meaning: The power card cut-out temperature has exceeded its upper limit.
checks: Check the ambient temperature and cabinet ventilation
Check fans and filters; clean heatsink airways
Compare the heatsink temperature in 16-34

faults.name: Drive initialized to default
faults.meaning: All parameters have been set back to factory defaults.
checks: Re-enter motor data and application settings
Restore a saved LCP copy if available (0-50)

faults.name: Auto DC braking
faults.meaning: Occurs on IT mains when the drive coasts and the DC link exceeds 830 V (400 V units) or 425 V (200 V units); the motor is feeding energy into the DC link. This function can be switched in 0-07.
checks: Check the mains type setting in 0-06
Review 0-07 Auto DC Braking
Check for overhauling load during coast

faults.name: Option detection
faults.meaning: The option has been removed successfully.
checks: Confirm the removal is intended, then reset

faults.name: Broken belt
faults.meaning: A broken belt or coupling is suspected.
checks: Inspect the belt or coupling
Review broken-belt settings in 22-6*

faults.name: Locked rotor
faults.meaning: The rotor is blocked.
checks: Check for a mechanical jam
Review locked rotor detection settings 30-22 and 30-23

faults.name: Position control fault
faults.meaning: A fault occurred in position control.
checks: Check position feedback and the position control settings

faults.name: Motor rotating
faults.meaning: A PM motor is rotating while AMA is being performed.
checks: Stop the motor and make sure it is not being turned by the load before running AMA

faults.name: Back EMF too high
faults.meaning: The back EMF of the PM motor is too high before starting.
checks: Make sure the motor is not rotating before the start command
Check the back EMF setting (1-40)

faults.name: STO internal fault
faults.meaning: 24 V DC is applied to only one of the two STO terminals (37 and 38), or a fault was detected in the STO channels. Both terminals must be powered and the discrepancy between the two signals must be under 12 ms. This alarm cannot be auto-reset through 14-20.
checks: Check that both terminals 37 and 38 are powered from 24 V DC
Check the timing difference between the two channels
Contact the local Danfoss supplier if it persists

faults.name: Not while running
faults.meaning: Display message: the parameter can only be changed when the motor is stopped.
checks: Stop the motor, then change the parameter

faults.name: Wrong password entered
faults.meaning: Display message shown when a wrong password is used to change a password-protected parameter.
checks: Enter the correct main menu password (0-60)

params.name: Language
params.range: [0] English, [1] Deutsch, [2] Francais, [3] Dansk, [4] Spanish, [5] Italiano, [28] Portuguese
params.desc: Sets the language of the LCP display texts.

params.name: Regional Settings
params.desc: Chooses kW or hp units for motor power entry (1-20) and sets the default motor frequency to 50 or 60 Hz. Cannot be changed while the motor runs.

params.name: Operating State at Power-up (Hand)
params.range: [0] Resume, [1] Forced stop, ref=old, [2] Forced stop, ref=0
params.default: [1] Forced stop, ref=old (parameter list table shows [0] Resume)
params.desc: Decides how the drive behaves after mains returns when it was in Hand mode: carry on running, stay stopped with the stored local reference, or stay stopped with the local reference cleared.

params.name: GridType
params.range: Supply options by voltage class (200-240, 380-440, 440-480 V), 50/60 Hz and IT-grid / Delta / standard type
params.desc: Tell the drive the actual supply voltage, frequency and earthing type. A wrong choice (especially IT grid) affects DC-link handling and overvoltage behaviour.

params.name: Auto DC Braking
params.desc: Protects against DC-link overvoltage when coasting on an IT grid. Only has effect when an IT-grid option is chosen in 0-06. Related to warning 87.

params.name: Active Set-up
params.range: [1] Set-up 1, [2] Set-up 2, [3] Set-up 3, [4] Set-up 4, [9] Multi Set-up
params.desc: Selects which of the four parameter set-ups controls the drive. Multi set-up lets digital inputs or the bus switch set-ups remotely.

params.name: Programming Set-up
params.desc: Picks the set-up you are editing, which may differ from the one currently running the drive.

params.name: Link Setups
params.desc: When linked, parameters that cannot be changed while running are copied between set-ups so a set-up change during operation is possible.

params.name: Application Selection
params.range: [0] None, [1] Simple Process Close Loop, [2] Local/Remote, [3] Speed Open Loop, [4] Simple Speed Close Loop, [5] Multi Speed, [6] OGD LA10, [7] OGD V210, [8] Hoist
params.desc: Loads a preset group of parameters for a typical application in one step. Check the resulting settings afterwards because many parameters change at once.

params.name: [Hand on] Key on LCP
params.desc: Enables or blocks the Hand On key, which prevents accidental local starts when disabled.

params.name: [Auto on] Key on LCP
params.desc: Enables or blocks the Auto On key on the LCP.

params.name: [Off/Reset] Key on LCP
params.desc: Controls whether the Off/Reset key can stop and reset the drive. Setting 7 leaves only the reset function active.

params.name: LCP Copy
params.range: [0] No copy, [1] All to LCP, [2] All from LCP, [3] Size indep. from LCP
params.desc: Copies parameters between the drive and the LCP. Saving to the LCP after commissioning gives you a backup, and loading from the LCP clones settings to another drive.

params.name: Set-up Copy
params.range: [0] No copy, [1]-[4] Copy from set-up 1-4, [9] Copy from Factory setup
params.desc: Copies a complete set-up (or the factory set-up) onto the set-up chosen in 0-11.

params.name: Main Menu Password
params.desc: Protects the Main Menu with a password. Zero disables the password.

params.name: Configuration Mode
params.range: [0] Open Loop, [1] Speed closed loop, [2] Torque closed loop, [3] Process Closed Loop, [4] Torque open loop, [7] Extended PID Speed OL
params.desc: Chooses the basic control principle used when a remote reference is active: plain speed control, or closed loop with feedback.

params.name: Motor Control Principle
params.desc: Selects the motor control method. U/f gives a simple voltage/frequency curve without slip or load compensation; VVC+ is the default vector method.

params.name: Torque Characteristics
params.range: [0] Constant torque, [1] Variable Torque, [2] Auto Energy Optim. CT, [3] Auto Energy Optim. VT
params.desc: Matches the drive to the load type. Variable torque (fans, pumps) and the auto-energy options reduce motor magnetisation at light load to save energy.

params.name: Clockwise Direction
params.desc: Reverses the meaning of clockwise so the motor direction can be changed without swapping motor wires. Cannot be changed while running.

params.name: Motor Control Bandwidth
params.default: [1] Medium (parameter list table says Size related)
params.desc: Trades dynamic response against smooth steady-state running.

params.name: Motor Construction
params.range: [0] Asynchron, [1] PM, non salient SPM, [3] PM, salient IPM
params.desc: Selects induction or permanent magnet motor type. Many other motor parameters depend on this choice.

params.name: Motor Power
params.range: Standard motor ratings in kW / hp, from 0.12 kW (0.16 hp) upward
params.desc: Motor rated power from the nameplate. Together with 1-22 to 1-25 it forms the motor data the drive needs.

params.name: Motor Voltage
params.desc: Rated motor voltage from the nameplate; check the star/delta connection that corresponds to the supply.

params.name: Motor Frequency
params.desc: Rated motor frequency from the nameplate. For 87 Hz operation also adapt 4-14 and 3-03. Cannot be changed while running.

params.name: Motor Current
params.desc: Rated motor current from the nameplate. It underlies torque estimation and the motor thermal protection, so a wrong value causes nuisance trips.

params.name: Motor Nominal Speed
params.desc: Rated motor speed from the nameplate. Used for slip compensation and other automatic motor compensation.

params.name: Motor Cont. Rated Torque
params.desc: Rated continuous torque of a PM motor from its nameplate. Only available with PM motor construction.

params.name: Automatic Motor Adaption (AMA)
params.range: [0] Off, [1] Enable complete AMA, [2] Enable reduced AMA
params.desc: Starts a self-measurement of motor parameters to tune the control. Terminal 27 must be active (not switched off with the default coast-inverse setting), and the motor should be cold. Failures show as alarms 50-58.

params.name: Stator Resistance (Rs)
params.desc: Stator winding resistance, from the motor datasheet or measured by AMA on a cold motor.

params.name: Rotor Resistance (Rr)
params.desc: Rotor resistance, from a datasheet or AMA on a cold motor. Default is calculated from nameplate data.

params.name: Stator Leakage Reactance (X1)
params.desc: Stator leakage reactance, from a datasheet or AMA on a cold motor.

params.name: Main Reactance (Xh)
params.desc: Main (magnetising) reactance of the motor, found by AMA on a cold motor or from the motor datasheet.

params.name: d-axis Inductance (Ld)
params.desc: d-axis inductance of a PM motor, from its datasheet or AMA on a cold motor.

params.name: q-axis Inductance (Lq)
params.desc: q-axis inductance of a PM motor, from its datasheet or AMA on a cold motor.

params.name: Motor Poles
params.desc: Total number of motor poles (not pole pairs), always even. Needed for correct speed calculation.

params.name: Back EMF at 1000 RPM
params.desc: Line-to-line voltage a PM motor generates when turned externally at 1000 RPM.

params.name: Motor Cable Length
params.desc: Length of the motor cable, used to compensate for cable effects. Set it correctly for long cables.

params.name: U/f Characteristic - U
params.desc: Voltage values at each of six frequency points of a custom U/f curve (array parameter).

params.name: U/f Characteristic - F
params.desc: Frequency points that define the custom U/f curve together with 1-55.

params.name: Low Speed Load Compensation
params.desc: Adjusts voltage compensation at low speed to improve load performance. Asynchronous motors only.

params.name: High Speed Load Compensation
params.desc: Adjusts voltage compensation at high speed to improve load performance. Asynchronous motors only.

params.name: Slip Compensation
params.desc: Trims slip compensation, which is calculated automatically from motor nominal speed, to allow for motor tolerance.

params.name: Slip Compensation Time Constant
params.desc: Reaction speed of slip compensation. Raise it if low-frequency resonance or hunting appears.

params.name: Resonance Dampening
params.desc: Damps high-frequency resonance of the motor; increase to reduce oscillation, in step with 1-65.

params.name: Min. Current at Low Speed
params.desc: Minimum motor current at low speed; raising it increases low-speed torque. Only active for PM motors.

params.name: Start Mode
params.range: [0] Rotor Detection, [1] Parking, [3] Rotor Last Position
params.desc: Start-up method for PM motors in VVC+, used when the motor may be free-running or stopped.

params.name: Start Delay
params.desc: Delays the start of acceleration. The function used during the delay is chosen in 1-72.

params.name: Start Function
params.range: [0] DC Hold/delay time, [1] DC-Brake/delay time, [2] Coast/delay time, [3] Start speed cw, [4] Horizontal operation, [5] VVC+ clockwise
params.desc: Chooses what the drive does during the start delay: DC hold, DC brake, coast, or special start-speed functions for hoists and cone-rotor motors.

params.name: Start Speed [Hz]
params.desc: Frequency the output jumps to at start when a start-speed function is selected in 1-72.

params.name: Start Current
params.desc: Extra current used at start with start-speed functions, for motors needing help to break away (e.g. cone rotor).

params.name: Function at Stop
params.range: [0] Coast, [1] DC hold / Motor Preheat, [3] Pre-magnetizing (options depend on motor construction)
params.desc: Chooses what the drive does after a stop command once speed has fallen to the level in 1-82.

params.name: Min Speed for Function at Stop [Hz]
params.desc: Output frequency below which the function chosen in 1-80 becomes active.

params.name: AC Brake Gain
params.desc: Strength of the AC brake. Higher values brake harder; 1.0 means no AC brake capability.

params.name: Motor Thermal Protection
params.range: [0] No protection, [1] Thermistor warning, [2] Thermistor trip, [3] ETR warning 1, [4] ETR trip 1, [22] ETR Trip - Extended Delay
params.desc: Selects how the motor is protected against overheating: using a PTC thermistor, or the drive's electronic thermal model. Leaving it at 0 gives no protection.

params.name: Thermistor Source
params.range: [0] None, [1] Analog Input 53, [2] Analog Input 54, [3] Digital input 18, [4] Digital input 19, [5] Digital input 32, [6] Digital input 33
params.desc: Tells the drive which terminal the motor PTC thermistor is wired to. Set the matching input mode first (5-00, 6-19, 6-29).

params.name: DC Hold/Motor Preheat Current
params.desc: Holding current for DC hold or motor preheating, as a percentage of rated motor current.

params.name: DC Brake Current
params.desc: Braking current for DC brake, as a percentage of rated motor current.

params.name: DC Braking Time
params.desc: How long DC brake current is applied after a stop. A value of 0 disables DC braking.

params.name: DC Brake Cut In Speed
params.desc: Frequency at which DC braking is switched in during a stop.

params.name: Brake Function
params.desc: Selects how regenerative energy is dealt with: no brake, a brake resistor, or AC braking.

params.name: Brake Resistor (ohm)
params.desc: Value of the connected brake resistor, used to monitor brake power.

params.name: Brake Power Limit (kW)
params.desc: Maximum power the brake resistor may dissipate, monitored over a 120 s window (see warning 26).

params.name: AC Brake, Max current
params.desc: Current limit during AC braking.

params.name: Over-voltage Control
params.desc: Lets the drive stretch the deceleration ramp automatically to avoid DC-link overvoltage trips.

params.name: Over-voltage Gain
params.desc: Tunes how strongly the over-voltage control reacts.

params.name: Release Brake Current
params.desc: Motor current that must be reached before a mechanical brake is released.

params.name: Activate Brake Speed [Hz]
params.desc: Frequency at which the mechanical brake is applied during stopping.

params.name: Activate Brake Delay
params.desc: Delay before the mechanical brake is applied after stopping.

params.name: Reference Range
params.desc: Selects whether references may be only positive or both positive and negative.

params.name: Minimum Reference
params.desc: Lowest reference value obtainable from all sources; defines the minimum speed or process value.

params.name: Maximum Reference
params.desc: Highest reference value obtainable by summing all references.

params.name: Reference Function
params.desc: Either adds external and preset references together or switches between them with a command or digital input.

params.name: Preset Reference
params.desc: Up to eight fixed references, selected by digital inputs or the bus, expressed as a percentage of the reference range.

params.name: Jog Speed [Hz]
params.desc: Fixed output frequency used while jog is active.

params.name: Preset Relative Reference
params.desc: Defines a percentage added to the actual reference to give a relative reference.

params.name: Reference 1 Source
params.range: [0] No function, [1] Analog Input 53, [2] Analog Input 54, [7] Frequency input 29, [8] Frequency input 33, [11] Local bus reference, [20] Digital pot.meter, [32] Bus PCD
params.desc: Chooses the first source of the speed/process reference.

params.name: Reference 2 Source
params.desc: Chooses the second reference source.

params.name: Reference 3 Source
params.desc: Chooses the third reference source.

params.name: Ramp 1 Ramp Up Time
params.desc: Acceleration time from 0 to the rated motor frequency (1-23). Too short a time can cause current limit or overcurrent.

params.name: Ramp 1 Ramp Down Time
params.desc: Deceleration time from rated motor frequency to 0. Too short a time can cause DC overvoltage unless a brake is fitted.

params.name: Ramp 2 Ramp Up Time
params.desc: Acceleration time for the second ramp, selectable by digital input.

params.name: Ramp 2 Ramp Down Time
params.desc: Deceleration time for the second ramp.

params.name: Jog Ramp Time
params.desc: Ramp time used when jogging.

params.name: Quick Stop Ramp Time
params.desc: Deceleration time used for a quick stop command.

params.name: Motor Speed Direction
params.desc: Allowed rotation directions. Must allow both directions if reversing is to be used.

params.name: Motor Speed Low Limit [Hz]
params.desc: Minimum output frequency during operation.

params.name: Motor Speed High Limit [Hz]
params.desc: Maximum output frequency the motor is allowed to run at; set it with the mechanical limits of the machine in mind.

params.name: Torque Limit Motor Mode
params.desc: Torque limit when driving the load. Reaching it gives warning/alarm 12.

params.name: Torque Limit Generator Mode
params.desc: Torque limit when the load drives the motor (regenerating).

params.name: Current Limit
params.desc: Output current limit. Reaching it gives warning/alarm 59.

params.name: Max Output Frequency
params.desc: Absolute upper limit on drive output frequency regardless of other settings; cannot exceed 10% of the switching frequency.

params.name: Torque Limit Factor Source
params.range: [0] No function, [2] Analog in 53, [4] Analog in 53 inv, [6] Analog in 54, [8] Analog in 54 inv, [18] Bus Control
params.desc: Scales the torque limits with an analog input or the bus.

params.name: Break Away Boost
params.desc: Provides extra starting torque for loads that are hard to break away.

params.name: Motor Feedback Loss Function
params.range: [0] Disabled, [1] Warning, [2] Trip, [3] Jog, [4] Freeze Output, [5] Max Speed, [6] Switch to Open Loop
params.desc: What to do if the feedback signal is lost in closed-loop speed control.

params.name: Warning Freq. Low
params.desc: Frequency below which a low-frequency warning is issued.

params.name: Warning Freq. High
params.desc: Frequency above which a high-frequency warning is issued.

params.name: Warning Current Low
params.desc: Motor current below which a low-current warning is issued; useful for detecting a lost load.

params.name: Warning Current High
params.desc: Motor current above which a high-current warning is issued.

params.name: Missing Motor Phase Function
params.desc: Enables detection of a missing motor phase, giving alarms 30-32.

params.name: Bypass Speed From [Hz]
params.desc: Start of a speed band the drive skips over to avoid mechanical resonance.

params.name: Bypass Speed To [Hz]
params.desc: End of the skipped speed band.

params.name: Digital Input Mode
params.desc: Sets the wiring logic of the digital inputs (PNP active at 24 V, NPN active at 0 V). Wrong setting makes inputs seem dead.

params.name: Terminal 27 Mode
params.desc: Selects whether terminal 27 acts as a digital input or output.

params.name: Terminal 18 Digital Input

faults.name: Overcurrent at constant speed
faults.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while running at steady speed, so the output was cut.
checks: Look for sudden load changes and remove them
Check motor leads for short circuit between phases
Check motor and cable for an earth fault
Check the motor is not seized or locked
If a PM motor is used, confirm its parameters were set and tuned correctly

faults.name: Overcurrent during deceleration
faults.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while slowing down.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Check motor leads for a short circuit and the motor/cable for an earth fault
Check the motor is not jammed

faults.name: Overcurrent during acceleration
faults.meaning: Output current spiked to roughly twice the inverter rating while speeding up.
checks: Lengthen the acceleration time
Reduce the torque boost setting if it is high
Check the motor is not locked and the wiring is sound
For a PM motor verify motor data and tuning

faults.name: Overcurrent in other conditions
faults.meaning: Overcurrent trip outside the accel, decel and constant-speed cases.
checks: Reduce the DC injection braking power if it is set high
Check output wiring and the motor for a short circuit or earth fault
Check for a locked motor

faults.name: Motor overload (electronic thermal)
faults.meaning: The built-in electronic thermal model decided the motor was overloaded. With the separated thermal setting (b910) this is the motor protection. Reset is refused for about 10 s after the trip.
checks: Reduce the load
Check the electronic thermal level (b012/b212) matches the motor nameplate current
Lengthen the acceleration time if starting torque is marginal
Wait about 10 seconds before resetting

faults.name: Braking resistor overload
faults.meaning: Regenerative braking circuit usage went above the limit set in b090.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Lengthen the duty cycle (fewer braking events per minute)
Check b090 and the braking resistor rating

faults.name: Overvoltage (DC bus)
faults.meaning: DC bus voltage rose above the trip level (about 400 V on 200 V class, 800 V on 400 V class) because of regeneration or high supply voltage.
checks: Lengthen the deceleration time
Check motor wiring/motor for an earth fault
Check whether the load drives the motor (overhauling) and reduce regeneration or add braking
Check the supply voltage; consider an AC reactor on the input

faults.name: EEPROM error
faults.meaning: Fault while accessing the internal EEPROM, often from noise or excessive temperature. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check for strong noise sources nearby and improve EMC measures
Check the heat sink is not clogged
Cycle power; if the error returns, initialise parameters (memory may be corrupt)

faults.name: Undervoltage
faults.meaning: DC bus voltage fell below the undervoltage level (about 173 V on 200 V class, 345 V on 400 V class).
checks: Check supply voltage
Check supply capacity is sufficient for the load/starting
Consider ageing of the DC bus capacitors

faults.name: Current detector error
faults.meaning: The inverter detected a fault in its current sensing circuit.
checks: Internal fault - the unit needs repair

faults.name: CPU error
faults.meaning: Malfunction or error in the internal CPU. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists after power cycling, the inverter is faulty - repair
If it persists, initialise parameters

faults.name: External trip
faults.meaning: A multi-function input programmed as EXT (12) turned ON.
checks: Check the external equipment wired to that input
Check wiring and the terminal contact logic (C011-C017)
Check for noise on the input wiring

faults.name: USP error
faults.meaning: Power was applied while a RUN command was already present, with the USP function enabled.
checks: Remove the RUN command before power-up
Check the RUN command wiring and source

faults.name: Ground fault
faults.meaning: An earth fault was detected between inverter output and motor at power-up. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check output wiring and motor insulation for an earth fault
Disconnect the motor leads and re-test to separate inverter from motor
Check the main circuit of the inverter (see maintenance section)

faults.name: Input overvoltage
faults.meaning: Supply voltage stayed high (DC bus about 390 V on 200 V class, 780 V on 400 V class) for 100 seconds.
checks: Lower the supply voltage / correct supply fluctuation
Install an AC reactor on the input

faults.name: Temperature sensor error
faults.meaning: The heat sink temperature sensing circuit reports an error such as a broken sensor line.
checks: Internal fault - the unit needs repair

faults.name: Overtemperature
faults.meaning: Main circuit temperature exceeded the allowed limit.
checks: Check the inverter is mounted vertically with proper clearances
Reduce ambient temperature
Check the cooling fan runs (set b092 to always on if needed) and its supply
Clean the heat sink fins

faults.name: CPU communication error
faults.meaning: Fault or malfunction in the internal CPU communication.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists, repair the inverter

faults.name: Main circuit error
faults.meaning: An error was detected on the main circuit board.
checks: Check for strong noise sources and improve EMC measures
If it persists, repair the inverter

faults.name: Analog current input error
faults.meaning: Excess current flowed into the FI analog current input terminal.
checks: Check FI wiring for a short circuit or wrong connection
If wiring is fine, the control board is faulty - repair

faults.name: Driver error
faults.meaning: The gate driver detected a momentary overcurrent (around 350% of rated), main-element overtemperature or driver supply drop. Cannot be reset by RS terminal or STOP/RESET key; power cycle is required.
checks: Check output wiring for a short circuit
Check motor and cables for an earth fault
Test the IGBT module for damage
Clean the heat sink fins

faults.name: Thermistor error
faults.meaning: The external thermistor input reads an abnormal motor temperature.
checks: Check the actual motor temperature
Check the thermistor and its wiring for damage
Separate thermistor wiring from noise sources
Check thermistor input settings (C005 = 19, C085)

faults.name: Brake error
faults.meaning: With brake control enabled (b120 = 01), the brake ON/OFF confirmation did not arrive within b124 after the release signal.
checks: Check the mechanical brake operates
Increase b124 if the time is too short
Check the brake confirmation input wiring (BOK)

faults.name: Emergency shutoff (safety input)
faults.meaning: The safety inputs GS1/GS2 were opened.
checks: Check GS1/GS2 wiring and the safety sequence
Check the GS input operation setting b145

faults.name: Low-speed overload
faults.meaning: The electronic thermal function detected an overload at extremely low speed (0.2 Hz or less); with the separated setting (b910) this is the inverter protection. The history may show a higher frequency.
checks: Reduce the load, particularly at very low speed
Check electronic thermal settings (b012, b910)

faults.name: Digital Operator connection error
faults.meaning: Communication with the remote operator 3G3AX-OP01 failed or the cable was disconnected (detection can be disabled with b165 = 02).
checks: Check or replace the operator cable
Review b165

faults.name: Modbus communication error
faults.meaning: A communication timeout occurred while C076 is set to trip.
checks: Check communication speed and settings match the master
Check wire length and cable quality
Check for a broken wire
Check the terminating resistor setting

faults.name: DriveProgramming program error
faults.meaning: Errors raised by the built-in DriveProgramming function (program faults).
checks: See the separate DriveProgramming manual for the cause of the specific code

faults.name: DriveProgramming user trip
faults.meaning: User-defined trips generated by a DriveProgramming program.
checks: See the DriveProgramming manual and the user program for the trip meaning

faults.name: Option unit error
faults.meaning: Error reported by an installed option unit (for example the EtherCAT unit).
checks: See the manual for the option unit installed

faults.name: Option communication timeout
faults.meaning: Communication between the inverter and the option unit timed out.
checks: Check the option unit is seated correctly and its fixing screws are tight
If properly mounted, the option unit may be faulty

faults.name: Encoder disconnection
faults.meaning: Measured motor speed stayed below the starting frequency (b082) for the P077 time while output was at or above creep speed P015; the real frequency monitor d008 is set to 0.
checks: Check encoder wiring for a break or wrong connection
Slightly raise P077 and P015

faults.name: Overspeed
faults.meaning: Motor speed from the encoder exceeded the P026 level (P026 not zero); d008 is set to 0.
checks: Check encoder wiring
Check the encoder pulse count setting (P011)
Check the load conditions and frequency setting F001
Adjust the overspeed level P026

faults.name: Position control range trip
faults.meaning: During simple position control the current position went outside the limits P072/P073.
checks: Check the current position and the limits P072/P073
Check position commands P060-P067
Check the origin

faults.name: STO self-diagnosis error
faults.meaning: A fault was found in the STO input terminals or internal safety circuit; independent of the b145 setting.
checks: Perform the periodic functional test of the safety function
Check for strong noise sources
Internal safety circuit may be faulty - repair

faults.name: Parameter conflict warning
faults.meaning: When one setting contradicts another (for example a frequency limit above the maximum frequency, or a start frequency above a limit) the PRG LED blinks and the RUN command is ignored. The latest warning code is stored in d090.
checks: Read d090 to see which parameter pair conflicts
Correct the settings: frequency upper/lower limits (A061/A062) vs maximum frequency (A004), start frequency (b082) vs limits and jogging, set frequency vs jump frequencies

params.name: Output frequency monitor
params.desc: Live output frequency; also the default screen after power-up.

params.name: Output current monitor
params.desc: Shows motor current as filtered by the inverter - first thing to check for load problems.

params.name: Run direction monitor
params.desc: Shows whether the inverter is running forward, stopped or reverse.

params.name: Multi-function input monitor
params.desc: Shows which control inputs the inverter sees as ON; use it to check wiring.

params.name: Multi-function output monitor
params.desc: Shows the state of the open-collector outputs and relay.

params.name: Real frequency monitor
params.desc: Actual speed measured by the encoder when feedback is used.

params.name: Output voltage monitor
params.desc: Voltage the inverter is putting out to the motor.

params.name: Input power monitor
params.desc: Electrical power drawn by the drive.

params.name: Total power ON time monitor
params.desc: Cumulative hours the drive has been powered.

params.name: Fin temperature monitor
params.desc: Heat sink temperature - useful when investigating E21.

params.name: Life assessment monitor
params.desc: Indicates whether the main capacitors or cooling fan have reached the end of expected life.

params.name: Inverter mode monitor
params.desc: Shows the active mode: induction normal load, induction light load, high-frequency or PM motor.

params.name: Frequency reference source monitor
params.desc: Tells you where the current frequency command is coming from.

params.name: RUN command source monitor
params.desc: Tells you which source is issuing the RUN command.

params.name: Fault counter
params.desc: How many trips have occurred.

params.name: Fault monitor 1 (latest) to 6 (d081-d086)
params.desc: Trip history with output frequency, current, DC bus voltage and run/power-on hours at the moment of the fault.

params.name: Warning monitor
params.desc: Latest parameter-conflict warning.

params.name: DC voltage monitor
params.desc: DC bus voltage - helps diagnose E07/E09.

params.name: Regenerative braking load rate monitor
params.desc: How hard the braking chopper is working.

params.name: Electronic thermal load rate monitor
params.desc: Percentage of the thermal overload budget used; near 100 means E05 is imminent.

params.name: Output frequency setting/monitor
params.desc: Frequency reference entered from the keypad; also shows the set speed.

params.name: 1st acceleration time 1
params.desc: Time to ramp up from zero to maximum frequency.

params.name: 2nd acceleration time 1
params.desc: Ramp-up time used when the second motor/setting set is selected.

params.name: 1st deceleration time 1
params.desc: Time to ramp down from maximum frequency to zero; too short can cause E07.

params.name: 2nd deceleration time 1
params.desc: Ramp-down time for the second setting set.

params.name: RUN direction selection
params.desc: Direction used when running from the keypad.

params.range: 00 operator volume, 01 terminal, 02 operator F001, 03 Modbus, 04 option, 06 pulse train, 07 DriveProgramming, 10 operation function

params.name: 2nd frequency reference selection
params.desc: Speed command source for the second setting set.

params.name: 1st RUN command selection
params.desc: Chooses where the start/stop command comes from.

params.name: 2nd RUN command selection
params.desc: Start/stop source for the second setting set.

params.name: 1st base frequency
params.desc: Frequency at which full motor voltage is reached; set to the motor nameplate frequency.

params.name: 2nd base frequency
params.desc: Base frequency for the second motor.

params.name: 1st maximum frequency
params.desc: Highest output frequency allowed.

params.name: 2nd maximum frequency
params.desc: Highest output frequency for the second set.

params.name: FV/FI selection
params.desc: Selects which analog inputs are switched by the AT terminal.

params.name: FV start frequency
params.desc: Frequency corresponding to the start of the analog voltage range.

params.name: FV end frequency
params.desc: Frequency corresponding to the end of the analog voltage range.

params.name: FV start ratio
params.desc: Input percentage where the FV start frequency applies.

params.name: FV end ratio
params.desc: Input percentage where the FV end frequency applies.

params.name: FV start selection
params.desc: Whether the output at the start of the range is A011 or zero.

params.name: Analog input filter
params.desc: Smooths noisy analog speed signals at the cost of response.

params.name: Multi-step speed selection
params.desc: Chooses binary or bit-type selection of preset speeds.

params.name: 1st multi-step speed reference 0
params.desc: Preset speed 0, which is also the keypad frequency.

params.name: Multi-step speed reference 1 (A021-A035: 1 to 15)

params.name: Jogging frequency
params.range: Start freq to 10.00 Hz (100.00 in HF mode)
params.desc: Speed used for jog operation.

params.name: Jogging stop selection
params.desc: How the motor stops after a jog: free-run, decel or DC brake, and whether jog is allowed while running.

params.name: 1st torque boost selection
params.desc: Selects manual or automatic low-speed torque boost.

params.name: 1st manual torque boost voltage
params.desc: Extra voltage at low frequency; raise carefully to improve starting torque.

params.name: 1st manual torque boost frequency
params.desc: Frequency up to which the manual boost is applied.

params.name: 1st control method
params.range: 00 constant torque VC, 01 reduced torque VP, 02 free V/f, 03 sensorless vector
params.desc: Selects the V/f pattern or sensorless vector control.

params.name: 2nd control method
params.desc: Control method for the second setting set.

params.name: 1st output voltage gain
params.desc: Scales the output voltage; reducing it can quiet an overexcited motor.

params.name: 1st automatic torque boost voltage compensation gain
params.desc: Tuning of the automatic boost voltage.

params.name: 1st automatic torque boost slip compensation gain
params.desc: Tuning of the automatic boost slip compensation.

params.name: DC injection braking selection
params.range: 00 off, 01 on, 02 at set freq only
params.desc: Enables DC injection braking at stop.

params.name: DC injection braking frequency
params.desc: Frequency below which DC braking starts during deceleration.

params.name: DC injection braking delay time
params.desc: Wait before DC braking begins.

params.name: DC injection braking power
params.desc: Strength of the braking current.

params.name: DC injection braking time
params.desc: How long DC braking lasts.

params.name: Startup DC injection braking power
params.desc: DC braking applied before starting, e.g. to stop a spinning load.

params.name: Startup DC injection braking time
params.desc: Duration of start-up DC braking.

params.name: 1st frequency upper limit
params.desc: Upper clamp on the frequency reference.

params.name: 1st frequency lower limit
params.range: 0.00 (off) or start freq to upper limit (Hz)

params.name: Jump frequency 1
params.desc: Centre of a speed band to skip, used to avoid mechanical resonance.

params.name: Jump frequency width 1
params.desc: Width of the skipped band around jump 1.

params.name: PID P gain
params.desc: Proportional gain of the PID loop.

params.desc: Integral time of the PID loop.

params.name: PID scale

params.name: PID feedback selection

params.desc: Which input carries the PID feedback.

params.name: 1st AVR selection
params.range: 00 always on, 01 always off, 02 off during decel
params.desc: Automatic voltage regulation mode, compensating supply voltage variation.

params.name: 1st motor rated voltage selection
params.desc: Set to the motor's rated voltage.

params.name: Operation mode selection
params.desc: Enables energy-saving operation.

params.name: 1st acceleration time 2
params.desc: Second ramp-up time used with 2CH or frequency switching.

params.name: 1st deceleration time 2
params.desc: Second ramp-down time.

params.name: 1st 2-step accel/decel selection

params.desc: How the second ramp times are selected.

params.name: Acceleration pattern selection
params.range: 00 line, 01 S-curve, 02 U-curve, 03 inverted U, 04 EL-S
params.desc: Shape of the acceleration ramp.

params.name: Deceleration pattern selection
params.range: 00 line, 01 S-curve, 02 U-curve, 03 inverted U, 04 EL-S
params.desc: Shape of the deceleration ramp.

params.name: FI start frequency
params.desc: Frequency at the start of the FI current input range.

params.name: FI end frequency
params.desc: Frequency at the end of the FI current input range.

params.name: FI start ratio
params.desc: Percent of input (4 mA is 20%) where the start frequency applies.

params.name: FI end ratio
params.desc: Percent of input where the end frequency applies.

params.name: FI start selection
params.desc: Output below the FI start point.

params.name: Acceleration curve parameter
params.desc: Curvature of the S-type acceleration.

params.name: Deceleration curve parameter

params.name: Frequency addition amount
params.desc: Fixed frequency added to the reference when the ADD input is on.

params.name: Deceleration stop frequency

params.name: PID sleep operation level
params.desc: Frequency below which PID sleep may begin.

params.desc: What the drive does after a brief power loss: trip or restart in some way.

params.name: Allowable power interruption time
params.desc: Longest power dip that the drive will ride through.

params.name: Restart standby time
params.desc: Wait before restart after a power interruption.

params.name: Undervoltage trip selection during stop
params.range: 00 off, 01 on, 02 off during stop and RUN-off decel stop
params.desc: Whether undervoltage trips when stopped.

params.name: Power interruption restart count
params.desc: Number of automatic restarts allowed after power dips.

params.name: Overvoltage/overcurrent restart selection
params.range: 00 trip, 01 0-Hz, 02 pull-in at shutoff, 03 trip after pull-in decel stop, 04 pull-in restart

params.name: Overvoltage/overcurrent restart count
params.desc: How many retries are allowed.

params.name: Overvoltage/overcurrent restart standby time
params.desc: Delay before an automatic retry.

params.name: 1st electronic thermal level
params.range: 0.20 x rated current to 1.00 x rated current (A)
params.desc: Motor overload trip current; set to the motor nameplate current.

params.name: 2nd electronic thermal level
params.desc: Thermal level for the second motor.

params.name: 1st electronic thermal characteristics selection
params.range: 00 reduced torque, 01 constant torque, 02 free setting
params.desc: Matches the thermal curve to the load type.

params.name: 1st overload limit selection
params.range: 00 off, 01 accel+constant, 02 constant only, 03 accel+constant (accelerate in regen)
params.desc: Enables current limiting that reduces frequency when current goes too high.

params.name: 1st overload limit level
params.range: 0.20 x rated to 2.00 x rated (A, normal load)
params.desc: Current threshold at which the limiter acts.

params.name: 1st overload limit parameter
params.desc: Deceleration time used while the limiter is active.

params.name: Overcurrent suppression selection
params.range: 00 off, 01 on, 02 on at reduced voltage startup
params.desc: Suppresses overcurrent trips by limiting the ramp.

params.name: Frequency pull-in restart level
params.desc: Current limit while pulling in to a spinning motor.

params.name: Frequency pull-in restart parameter
params.desc: Deceleration rate during pull-in.

params.name: Starting frequency selection at pull-in restart
params.range: 00 frequency at interruption, 01 maximum, 02 set frequency
params.desc: Where the search for a spinning motor starts.

params.name: Soft lock selection

params.name: Motor cable length
params.desc: Cable length parameter used by the inverter's control.

params.name: RUN time/power ON time detection level
params.desc: Threshold for the RNT/ONT maintenance signals.

params.name: RUN direction limit selection
params.desc: Blocks one rotation direction.

params.name: Reduced voltage startup selection
params.desc: Slows voltage build-up at start to reduce inrush.

params.name: Display selection

params.name: Initial screen selection

params.name: Torque limit 1 (forward power running)

params.name: Normal/light load selection

params.name: Deceleration stop on power interruption selection

params.name: Analog operation level at FV disconnection

params.name: Analog operation level at FI disconnection
params.desc: Speed level used if the FI signal is lost.

params.name: Ambient temperature
params.desc: Ambient temperature used for life estimation.

params.name: Integrated power clear
params.desc: Resets the kWh counter.

params.name: Starting frequency
params.desc: Frequency at which output begins at start.

params.name: Carrier frequency
params.desc: PWM switching frequency; high values reduce motor noise but increase heat and leakage and need derating.

params.name: Frequency conversion coefficient

params.name: STOP key selection

params.name: Free-run stop selection

params.desc: How the drive restarts after a free-run stop is released.

params.name: Automatic carrier reduction
params.desc: Lowers carrier frequency to avoid overheating.

params.name: Usage rate of regenerative braking
params.desc: Duty rating of the braking resistor; exceeding it trips E06.

params.name: Stop selection

params.name: Cooling fan operation
params.range: 00 always, 01 only when running, 02 by fin temperature

params.desc: DC bus voltage where braking resistor turns on.

params.name: Braking resistor value

params.name: Ground fault detection selection

params.name: GS input operation selection
